generation.instructions: Generate one untouched image-model result for a controlled character-pose experiment. Treat the ordered existing-frame and skeleton pair as the exact mapping between this character and the skeleton convention. Preserve the mouse identity, proportions, costume, palette, line quality, viewing direction, and scale. Follow the target skeleton for the pelvis, spine, head, both arms, both legs, and feet. requests.composed_prompt:
Generate one untouched image-model result for a controlled character-pose experiment. Treat the ordered existing-frame and skeleton pair as the exact mapping between this character and the skeleton convention. Preserve the mouse identity, proportions, costume, palette, line quality, viewing direction, and scale. Follow the target skeleton for the pelvis, spine, head, both arms, both legs, and feet. Use the image-generation tool once and return its native pixels without any post-processing.

Negative requirements:
Do not copy the example pose. Do not omit, merge, or invent limbs. Do not draw skeleton lines, labels, text, a sprite sheet, a turnaround, scenery, shadows, or extra characters. Do not use ImageMagick, sips, Python imaging libraries, resizing, recanvasing, recoloring, quantization, or any other post-processing.

Reference inputs:
Reference 1 (subject-identity): preserve this subject's identity, proportions, design, palette, and identifying landmarks; do not copy the reference layout or pose.
Reference 2 (subject-identity): preserve this subject's identity, proportions, design, palette, and identifying landmarks; do not copy the reference layout or pose.
Reference 3 (pose): use only its pose, facing, limb geometry, and ground contact; do not copy its appearance, line style, or background.
Reference 4 (pose): use only its pose, facing, limb geometry, and ground contact; do not copy its appearance, line style, or background.

Subject request:
Draw the same right-facing mouse in the green hooded coat, red scarf, brown belt, brown boots, and long tail in the target running pose. Keep the character design identical to the matched existing frame while changing the complete body pose to follow the target skeleton. Use a plain white background.

The four reference images are ordered: (1) approved character identity, (2) an existing frame of that character, (3) the skeleton matched to image 2, and (4) the target skeleton. Images 2 and 3 define how this skeleton maps to the character. Draw the character from image 2 in image 4's pose.
Animation frame 4 of 12. Render exactly one fresh right-facing character image. Do not return a sheet, turnaround, wireframe, skeleton, or edited reference board.

raw_outputs.revised_prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: single animation frame, frame 4 of 12, square PNG
Primary request: Generate exactly one fresh image of the same right-facing mouse character from Images 1 and 2, redrawn in the complete target running pose from Image 4.
Input images: Image 1 = approved character identity reference. Image 2 = approved existing character frame and the exact character whose design must be preserved. Image 3 = skeleton matched to Image 2, defining the exact mapping between this character's anatomy/costume and the skeleton convention. Image 4 = target skeleton; use only its facing, pelvis, spine, head, arm, leg, foot, and ground-contact geometry.
Scene/backdrop: plain solid white background only.
Subject: one small right-facing anthropomorphic mouse wearing the identical deep green hooded coat, red scarf, brown belt with small gold buckle, brown boots, and long thin tail shown in Images 1 and 2. Preserve mouse identity, head and ear shapes, muzzle, nose, proportions, costume construction, palette, pixel-art line quality, viewing direction, and character scale.
Style/medium: polished retro pixel-art animation frame matching Images 1 and 2 exactly in pixel density, crispness, outlines, shading, and color treatment.
Composition/framing: 1:1 canvas; one complete full-body character centered with comfortable white margin. Match Image 4's pose exactly: right-facing running stride, torso lean and spine placement, head position, both arms with their elbow/wrist geometry, both legs with their knee/ankle geometry, both boots/feet, pelvis position, and ground contact. Use Images 2 and 3 as the ordered anatomical mapping that explains how the character is fitted onto the skeleton, then transfer that mapping faithfully to Image 4.
Constraints: Preserve every identifying landmark and costume detail. The result must visibly have exactly one head, two ears, two arms, two hands, two legs, two booted feet, and one tail, all anatomically distinct and connected. Change the complete pose from Image 2 to Image 4; do not copy Image 2's pose. Render exactly one isolated character image.
Avoid: skeleton lines or joints, guides, labels, any text, sprite sheet, turnaround, wireframe, reference board, scenery, props, cast shadows, ground line, extra characters, extra or missing limbs, merged limbs, invented limbs, cropped anatomy, transparent/checkered background, blur, anti-aliased painterly rendering, or any deviation from the approved character design.

- Reference 1: approved subject identity. Preserve the mouse's exact identity, proportions, costume design, palette, pixel-art line quality, viewing direction, scale, and identifying landmarks. Do not copy its pose or layout.
- Reference 2: existing animation frame of the same character and the character-side half of the exact character-to-skeleton mapping. Preserve its exact character design and right-facing direction. Do not copy its pose.
- Reference 3: skeleton matched exactly to reference 2; together references 2 and 3 define how every skeleton joint and segment maps onto this character's pelvis, spine, head, arms, legs, and feet. Use only to understand that mapping, never as the output pose or appearance.
- Reference 4: target skeleton. Use only its complete pose, facing, limb geometry, and ground contact. This is the pose the character must adopt.

Follow reference 4 for pelvis position and tilt, red spine angle, head/neck placement, both shoulders, both elbows, both wrists/hands, both hips, both knees, both ankles, both feet, and ground contact. Preserve all limbs: exactly two arms, two hands, two legs, two feet, one head, one tail. The pose is a distinct running stride and must not copy the example pose in reference 2 or the skeleton pose in reference 3.
Style/medium: crisp handcrafted retro pixel art matching references 1 and 2 exactly, including sprite proportions, pixel density, outline weight, selective highlights, shading clusters, and limited muted palette. Keep the same character scale within the square frame.
Composition/framing: one fully visible character centered with comfortable margins; right-facing; plain pure white background; no cropping.
Constraints: preserve mouse identity, body proportions, costume, palette, facial profile, hood, scarf, belt, boots, tail, right-facing view, pixel line quality, and apparent scale. The result should look like the next authentic frame from the same animation.
Avoid: do not copy the example pose; no omitted, merged, duplicated, or invented limbs; no skeleton lines, joint markers, guides, labels, text, border, sprite sheet, turnaround, wireframe, reference board, scenery, props, shadows, ground line, extra characters, watermark, blur, antialias-heavy painting, or non-pixel-art rendering.
